The pedestrian’s statement is admissible as an excited utterance because it was made immediately after the accident while the pedestrian was still under the stress of observing it, and the declarant’s unavailability or lack of identification does not bar admission under that exception. It is not admissible as a present sense impression only, since that exception does not require the declarant to be identified or available for cross-examination.  
CONFIDENCE: 70
